subject.title: fix(deepgram): reject malformed and non-http(s) realtime base URL overrides

question: Should shipped Deepgram configurations with malformed or non-HTTP(S) `baseUrl` values now fail immediately with an actionable error instead of reaching the existing downstream URL failure or unusable transport mapping?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but repository policy treats stricter validation of a shipped provider configuration surface as an explicit compatibility choice.

options.title: Accept fail-fast validation
options.body: Treat HTTP(S) as the supported base-origin contract and land the clearer immediate rejection for invalid explicit values.

options.title: Preserve legacy acceptance
options.body: Keep the current permissive behavior or add a migration path if maintainers consider non-HTTP(S) or malformed historical values a supported upgrade contract.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-fast validation
recommendation.body: Treat HTTP(S) as the supported base-origin contract and land the clearer immediate rejection for invalid explicit values.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the Deepgram provider and are the strongest available feature-history owner for its configuration contract.
